steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease or line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Combine flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, and salt together in a bowl.
Cream sugar with butter. Beat in persimmons and egg. Add flour mixture and mix until combined. Stir in chopped nuts.
Drop by teaspoonfuls, 2 inches apart, onto the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven for 12 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Soft Persimmon Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This is a tasty recipe for soft persimmon cookies. These cake-like cookies are wonderfully sweet and delicious; a great use of autumn persimmons.
raw_recipe.name: Soft Persimmon Cookies

review.reviewBody: Very good recipe! I made this recipe last night for dance class potluck and everyone devoured them so...I made them again today. Substitutions made: add 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1/2 tsp lemon extract, used only 1/2c. nuts (pecans) instead. *NOTE* Persimmons are not always available year-round so I like to buy lots, puree them and freeze - 2 persimmons equals about 1c. puree. Doing this will allow you to make yummy, comforting persimmon desserts all year long! OH YEAH...first time I made with half splenda/half sugar and it was fine. Non-diabetics enjoyed w/o noticing diff. - many even begged for recipe!
Delicious as is. Then I made a second batch with 1/2 sugar, 1/2 molasses and added raisins. Lightly iced with orange zest icing. Wow!!

I love this recipe! I add 1/2 cup golden raisins, 1/2 cup dried cranberries, and 1 cup oats for some additional flavor. Also, 1/2 applesauce can be substituted for the persimmons when they are not in season. If you add the extra fruit and oats, double the cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg. DELICIOUS! These can also be tossed into a 9x13 pyrex and cooked as bars instead of cookies.

Not a pretty looking cookie, but very tasty. It even seems to get better after a day or so in the cookie tin. I never had that experience with a cookie before. But the flavors of the spices seem to settle in more and the cookie stays wonderfully moist and chewy. The only changes I made were to use 1 tsp. of allspice instead of the cloves and nutmeg. Also, in my oven, the first batch got a bit burned on the bottom at 375, so I turned the oven down to 350 for the rest. That worked perfectly.

I used 1/2 cup more chucky pulp for a fruiter cookie. I used a teaspoon of vanilla. I refrigerated my dough before cooking. Then added raisins and pecans in some as well as just walnuts in others. I like the walnuts but I don't like sweet desserts. I made about 8 dozen and some were gifts but family and company ate them very quickly. Great with coffee in AM.

These are fabulous cookies! I had roasted persimmons with maple syrup and brown sugar the night before so I used the puree I had made from that. I also substituted 3/4 cup honey for the white sugar. Also baked on a Silpat for about 10-11 minutes. Will definitely be making these again!

These cookies were quite enjoyable. I did make a few adjustments to my liking. I used gluten-free flour instead. I reduced sugar amount to 1/4 cup of cane sugar, but added a handful of raisins to off-set the sweetness. I also used 2 full cups of persimmon pulp. The sweetness came out perfect for me. The clove and nutmeg flavor really came through and I did taste the persimmon too. I will lessen the nutmeg to 1/4 tsp next time. Maybe it'll bring more of the persimmon flavor out. The cookies did not harden, but were nice and moist. And because I used a different type of flour, the cookies did not flatten out either. They were bumpy and odd-shaped. None the less, they were great. The flavors were similar to the persimmon bread I made, just in a cookie form.

I looked for a "small batch" recipe & a few ccame up but being a baker, I knew they would be dry. Persimmon cookies aren't supposed to be dry. Due to the moisture in the persimmon, this is one of the most moist fruits you can bake with, rendering super moist cookies & cakes. I came upon this recipe & compared it to my granma's which I was trying to replicate only make them moist as Great-Grandma made them. There was a long-time feud between the two so asking for Great-Grandma's recipe was out of the question. My mission led me here. 
I baked the cookies for 13 minutes knowing I could bake longer but once too hard, they were a goner. 13 minutes was good. I could have baked only 11-12 & that too would have been good. Let the cookies set up on the baking sheet for about 3-5 minutes once removed from the oven to "finish" baking. I used toasted almonds & pecans. Both are really tasty. I've added walnuts in the past & that is a treat as well. Some folks like to add raisins. I'm not a fan of cooked raisins so those were not added. I didn't add ginger because the combo of that with the other spices makes the flavor reminiscent of pumpkin pie & these deserve their own flavor. I added a bit more cloves because I like a spiced cookie. These aren't overly sweet like chocolate chip cookies so if you're looking for something over the top sweet, scroll along or add frosting. Vanilla cream cheese is delightful atop these. 
In short, follow the directions & bake less time vs more because yo

I baked the first batch at 375 and they were too done so after that I baked them at 350. These cookies are delicious, especially if you would like to incorporate a few add-ons the family craves. Enjoy with tea, coffee or milk:)
I also decided to buy extra persimmons now that they are in season to mash and freeze for future recipes. I freeze them in batches of 2 persimmons in each Freezer Ziplock.
I liked these a lot. Made a yogurt lemon frosting to drizzle over. I gave them 4 stars because I tweaked the recipe a little. Added 1/2 tsp vanilla. Tasty and the kids gobbled them up!

Change the recipe a little added a 1cup of Almond meal/flour and 
1-1/2 cup of flour, one egg, 1/2 cup butter, cinnamon, nutmeg, dash of salt, baking soda and baking powder about a 1/4cup of sundried cranberry and sliced almonds. Baked for 15 min @ 375.

I made it today and the only changes I made was that I used Allspice instead of cloves and I used a Tablespoon of orange juice. They were delicious and moist! I will make this again next year, only I’ll use orange zest rather than orange juice. Thank you for sharing this recipe.

I made a mistake and added the sugar to the dry ingredients. So I puréed the persimmons in the food processor, added chunks of room temperature butter and puréed as well, it didn’t look as good, not so emulsified, but then I added the egg and it all came together quickly. With haste, I added to the dry ingredients and mixed until it just was mixed. These were the lightest persimmon cookies I have ever tasted, will always do it this way from now on.
The batch size is for very tiny cookies. But they taste amazing

Glad another reviewer posted amount of persimmon needed! (One cup!) Excellent recipe, cookies so good I had to freeze them to stop eating them. Reduced sugar to 3/4 ( half brown, half white) and added tsp vanilla. Persimmon perfection! I added a glaze of 1c powdered sugar/2 tbsp lemon juice for a little extra pizzazz
I make this recipe every season and they are cakey and delicious every time

I make these every year! Most recipes are basically same. They are moist chewy cookies not hard. I do mine with pecans and cruising. Delicious and always better the next day. Don't be alarmed, they do change color with each day. Make sure to place in a tight lid container. Yummy enjoy!!

Easy and delish! The only comment I have is the ingredients should show the measurement for the persimmons. Another review noted 2 persimmons is 1 cup puree. I was glad to see that because my persimmons were small.

I made a double recipe and used 4 persimmons that pureed came out to 2 cups. I cut down on the amount of cloves and nutmeg because last year my cookies had an overwhelming spice flavor and this batch was perfect. They have a cake like consistency which is exactly how I wanted them to be. This will be my go to recipe for persimmon cookies from now on.
Very tasty everyone love it can stop eating they are so good .
